title: Human rights
examples: What is the difference between a right and a responsibility?
Where did the Universal Declaration of Human Rights come from?
Can you give an example of a responsibility I have as a student?

explain.say: Today we will learn about human rights and our responsibilities.
The Universal Declaration sets out basic rights for all people.

items: No one can be discriminated against

explain.say: One right is the right to life and personal safety for everyone.
Another right is the right to education for every single child.
Remember that rights come with responsibilities to others too.
If you have the right to learn, you have the responsibility to study hard.

draw.text: Right to Learn = Duty to Study

faq.q: What is the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
faq.a: It is a document adopted by the United Nations. It sets out fundamental rights that should be enjoyed by all people. It is also known as the UDHR.
asks: Where do human rights come from?
What is the declaration of human rights?

faq.q: Are human rights the same everywhere in the world?
faq.a: The core rights are considered universal, meaning they apply to everyone regardless of where they live. However, how they are practiced can differ.
asks: Do all countries have the same rights?

faq.q: What is the difference between a right and a responsibility?
faq.a: A right is something you are entitled to receive, like education. A responsibility is an action you must take, like respecting others.
asks: What is the difference between a right and a duty?
Can I have rights without responsibilities?
If I have a right, do I have a responsibility?

faq.q: Can I lose my human rights?
faq.a: In theory, no, as they are inherent to being human. However, governments can sometimes restrict them under certain laws.
asks: Can my rights be taken away?

faq.q: Is the Universal Declaration a law?
faq.a: It is a declaration, which means it is a statement of ideals and moral standards. While not all countries have signed it into law, it guides international law.
asks: Do countries have to follow it?

facts: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in Paris in 1948.
It states that all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.
Fundamental rights include the right to life, freedom from torture, and freedom of opinion.
Every right comes with a corresponding responsibility to uphold the rights of others.

quiz.say: If a government stops you from speaking your mind, which right is being violated?
quiz.why: The right to freedom of expression protects your ability to share your thoughts and ideas safely.

wrong.0: This is about learning, not speaking out.
wrong.1: This is about physical safety, not speech.
wrong.2: Equality means fairness, but speech is a specific right.

quiz.say: When you see litter on the ground, what responsibility are you showing?
quiz.why: Taking care of shared spaces is a responsibility to the community.

wrong.1: This action is physical, not verbal.
wrong.2: This is an action of demanding, not caring for.
wrong.3: This is failing in a responsibility.

quiz.say: Which concept means that all people have worth simply because they are human?
quiz.why: Dignity means you have worth just by existing as a person.

wrong.0: Rights are not granted by law, they are inherent.
wrong.1: While society agrees on rights, the worth is deeper than that.
wrong.3: Status can be gained or lost, unlike inherent worth.
